gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a measured lip-sync delay for any product it recommended. GadgetReview measured the Sony HT-S100F at 62 ms over HDMI ARC and 70 ms over optical. It measured the original Bose SoundLink Flex at 109 ms (Android) and 236 ms (iOS) over Bluetooth, so the wired soundbar is about 1.8 to 3.8 times quicker.
standout_why: I compared against the cited itechguides how-to (upgrade-your-tv-experience...), the itechguides 5-speakers list and the geekchamp 5-soundbars list (the top results). The cited What Hi-Fi best-soundbars page did not render, so I couldn't check it. The itechguides how-to says Bluetooth adds delay but gives no millisecond figures. The itechguides and geekchamp lists give only generic Bluetooth figures (about 150 ms, or 40-50 ms with aptX Low Latency), credited to PCWorld via The Product Analyst, and Wirecutter bass SPL for Vizio, TCL and Samsung Q990H bars. None of them has a measured latency, max volume or bass roll-off for the HT-S100F, HT-SD40, HW-B630F or SoundLink Flex.
decides: It supports ChatGPT's advice to use a cabled soundbar over HDMI ARC rather than a Bluetooth speaker. The budget pick (HT-S100F) measured 62 ms over ARC. The portable Bose Flex measured 109-236 ms over Bluetooth, which is roughly 1.8-3.8 times the soundbar's figure. The comparison is only directional: the Bose was tested on the original model, paired to a phone rather than a TV, and the two products had different test setups. Over Bluetooth the HT-S100F supports only SBC (no aptX Low Latency), so wireless use doesn't avoid the lag. The answer to ChatGPT's follow-up question ('Bluetooth only?') should push toward 'a cable is fine'.
